correctness.rationale: Classify chord-containing perfect matchings by monomer-dimer tilings of cyclic n columns; each domino replaces two chords with two perimeter edges via a single alternating four-cycle, connecting the whole tiling sector. Even n has no outside configurations; odd n has two all-perimeter matchings with zero chords, while every tiling-sector matching has odd chord count. For any simple cycle with an odd number r of antipodal chords, edge-increment closure modulo 2n forces >=n perimeter edges, giving length >=n+r>=n+1. Exactly one alternating perimeter semicircle of length n exists for each of n antipodal chords from each all-perimeter matching. This proves Lconn=4 for even n and n+1 for odd, with exactly n first threshold neighbors per extreme (2n incident bridges total). Independent direct perfect-matching enumeration and flip connectivity for n=4..11 confirmed 1/3 component parity at length four, 1 component at threshold, and extreme degrees n at odd n.

originality.rationale: The tiling-sector Lucas-cube representation, known number of matchings and four-cycle component structure are background, not asserted new. Ito et al. 2019 study shortest reconfiguration under unrestricted alternating cycles and do not give the sharp allowable cycle-length threshold for this special graph in inspected full text. Lekshmi and West calculate matching counts, while later Resultary Möbius-ladder papers concern homology actions rather than one-flip connectivity. The parity-dependent exact threshold and n first-bridge count are not implied merely by these statements; a specialized dimer flip/resonance paper could still subsume them.
residual_risks: Specialized dimer-resonance literature may already characterize the n+1 threshold under a different definition.
The result excludes M6=K3,3 and allows only single alternating simple cycles, not simultaneous disjoint flips.
Finite enumerations n<=11 corroborate, not replace, the all-n winding proof.
